en.name: Dionysius
en.summary: A pope who reorganized the Roman church once the Valerian persecution had ended and worked to correct an overcorrection against the heresy of Modalism.
en.body: Dionysius became pope once the persecution that had killed his predecessor Sixtus II had subsided, and much of his decade-long reign was occupied with rebuilding the Roman church's structures and finances. He also intervened theologically against Dionysius of Alexandria, a bishop whose vigorous arguments against Modalism had, in Rome's judgment, swung too far toward describing the Father and Son as entirely separate beings — an early skirmish in the long doctrinal process that would eventually produce the Nicene formulation of the Trinity.
